description: A glyph at a size, inheriting its colour. Spectrum's smallest leaf: 36 of its 84 components depend on it.

curated.by: read from @adobe/spectrum-wc 2.0.0-beta.6 (dist/stylesheets/_lit-styles/icon-base.js) and its shipped type declarations

figma.notes: Spectrum publishes no Icon component set. The glyphs live in the separate S2 / Icons library as individual components; the size and colour behaviour is CSS only. Still the only contract in either system with no design anchor.

props.name: size
props.notes: Five rungs, one more than the other components: the icon adds xs.

props.name: accessibleLabel
props.notes: When empty the host is marked aria-hidden and the glyph is decorative; when set the host is exposed as an image with that label.

slot.name: glyph
slot.notes: The glyph itself. Spectrum ships these as a separate package; the manifest is built from it, not authored.

notes: Decorative by default: the root sets pointer-events none and the glyph carries no accessible name.
A meaningful icon needs a name on the element that owns the meaning, not on the glyph.

decisions.question: Spectrum ships no Icon component set in Figma, so this contract has code evidence only. Accept a code-first contract, or wait for a design anchor that may never exist?
decisions.fix: If Spectrum later publishes an Icon set, re-anchor and re-extract.
decisions.evidence: S2 / Web lists 142 component sets and none is Icon.

decisions.question: Spectrum's tokens carry a scale axis (medium and large) that S2A does not have; the same token resolves to 20px and 24px. Which scale does adobe.com bind to?
decisions.fix: If a surface needs large scale, the token directory gains a second mode rather than the contract gaining a prop.

decisions.question: Which package is Spectrum 2's Icon?
decisions.decision: The contract describes @adobe/spectrum-wc. Icon has no module of its own beyond a slot and a size box; its stylesheet is shared, at dist/stylesheets/_lit-styles/icon-base.js.
decisions.evidence: Icon.js imports icon-base.js for its only styles and renders a single default slot.

decisions.question: Every rule in the icon stylesheet is :host or ::slotted — there is not one class in it.
decisions.chose: Declare swc-Icon as the root class and re-express the host rules on it
decisions.fix: If the generated component becomes a custom element, drop the class and inherit the host rules.
decisions.evidence: icon-base.css is :host, :host([size]), and svg,::slotted(*) only. The class is ours, which is why the anatomy cannot be checked against the stylesheet.

decisions.question: How does a consumer resize or recolour the icon?
decisions.decision: Upstream exposes three custom properties on the host and derives everything else from them, so the size prop and a direct override reach the same place.
decisions.evidence: icon-base.css declares all three on :host with the size attribute switching the first two.

decisions.question: Every glyph rendered in its own colour instead of the component's.
decisions.chose: Map the artwork's own hook to currentColor on the part that holds the glyph
decisions.decision: Spectrum's workflow SVGs paint with fill="var(--iconPrimary, #222)" rather than currentColor, so with nothing defining that property every glyph fell back to #222 regardless of the colour around it. Setting --iconPrimary to currentColor on the icon part makes a glyph follow its component, and leaves the property available to anyone who wants a different colour.
decisions.fix: none. The alternative was rewriting 396 vendored SVGs, which would mean editing artwork we do not own.
decisions.evidence: All 396 entries in spectrum-icons.json carry var(--iconPrimary, #222); all 26 in our own s2a-icons.json use currentColor. Measured: the badge's text was #ffffff while its glyph painted #222222.
